> A wristwatch for elder people that also measures heart rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature with sensors connected to a ESP32-WROOM-32 38-pin dev board. It uses the board's built-in Wi-Fi for the time syncronization and to send alerts to nearby familiars If any value is not adequate. Since it's built for elder people it will have large buttons and just a few functions that are easy to comprehend. Useful If you have familiars that want to check their vitals at any moment of the day while also getting to know when they should take their medicine.

Finally looked into the specific parts and had to discard a few parts like the TMP117 and MAX30205 to replace them with available ones in peruvian electronics shops like the DS18B20 for temperature and the MAX30102 for the heart rate:

### 2026-10-03 — SaludWatch - 10/03/26 - Finally figured out the final parts and made a schematic using KiCad!

**6h**

SaludWatch - 10/03/26 - Finally figured out the final parts and made a schematic using KiCad!

(October 3)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/7bbfb0dac93c0093ff2add5df6be82ae07696b2036fb313eb17a091c60fbde27.png)
After a few hours I finally managed to get the final list for the project! Replaced the ESP32-C3 Super Mini for a ESP32-WROOM-32, and had to add the small boost converter MT3608 for the microcontroller to work with the 3.7V battery.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/1d9a7aed8e112fe9b10c884037eae2f82d28b27b490abb4692ba5fe1d2e41396.png)
Also included a Multimeter to calibrate the volts of the MT3608 and for safety reasons.

Worked on the KiCad schematic, took me a really good time to comprehend what symbols to add but I managed it! Also, pointed out the wiring with labels since standard wires take too much space. Faced some problems with the pin names and reference names covering too much, though I managed to find the option to hide them after some exploring. Also improved the organization in my repository added the schematic, going to update README.md soon, weekends are such great days to work on this project :)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/8gj7S6WIDaEIJSjTsLHoa4RS9wzwJHca/a587769cab8fa96bed7e9463f253d234bf191f8606eb6c1c73dcdcf85de2456e.png)

Here's the features in a list since writing beneath each pic would just take too long:

1.Here's the shelf plates, they are removable and are supported by the internal ledges in the base, each plate have a coin-shaped slot so wires can pass between the decks

2.Here's the base part of the case, it has port openings for the TP4056 micro-USB charger, ESP32 USB-C, a slot for the slide switch lever and a hole for the DS18B20 cable. If you've noticed, at the sides there's two lug straps, those are for the watch straps, part of the design! You can also see both internal ledges in this picture.

3.And finally the grand... Lid! I'm really proud of it, not just for the cutouts for the OLED, buttons and buzzers, but for it's ability to actually fit in the base! The ring under it does the magic.
